rows.description: A student is drawn to a classmate's humour and confidence and imagines a future from a few conversations. Infatuation fills in the blanks generously, so the person seen is partly the person wished for.
graph_context: next stage: Approach and uncertainty

rows.description: He replies to her stories, suggests coffee and reads her texts many times. Under the play is fear of rejection, and small signals such as reply speed feel enormously important.
graph_context: previous stage: Attraction and idealising
next stage: Getting to know the real person
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: fear

rows.subtype: Stage 3: Getting to know the real person [Actor]
rows.description: As they meet more they see habits, moods and differences in values. The glow fades a little, and the important question shifts from "do I like how this feels?" to "do I like who this is?".
graph_context: previous stage: Approach and uncertainty
next stage: The exclusivity question
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: One says "I would like us to be exclusive. Where do you stand?" Asking directly risks a no but ends weeks of guessing, and the answer, whichever it is, lets each act on facts.
graph_context: previous stage: Getting to know the real person
next stage: Meeting families and worlds
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: A friend notices them adjusting to each other's friends, food and family expectations. In many Indian families the question of caste, religion or a future household appears early and tests whether the couple can face the outside together.
graph_context: previous stage: The exclusivity question
next stage: A grounded commitment
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: They commit after seeing each other in stress as well as in joy, and speak honestly about goals. Commitment is a decision made with open eyes, not a feeling that simply arrives.
graph_context: previous stage: Meeting families and worlds
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: joy

rows.description: A young professional meets someone through friends or a matchmaking family. Attraction is present but tempered by questions on career, city and readiness, so excitement and caution share the same evening.
graph_context: next stage: Building routine and closeness
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: excitement, resentment

rows.description: They text morning to night, share meals and start planning weekends. Small acts of dependability such as remembering a deadline matter more now than grand gestures.
graph_context: previous stage: Spark with practical eyes
next stage: First real friction
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: A disagreement over money, time with parents or work travel reveals different expectations. How each behaves in the first real disagreement says more about the future than the honeymoon months.
graph_context: previous stage: Building routine and closeness
next stage: Fear of loss of freedom
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtype: Stage 4: Fear of loss of freedom [Actor]
rows.description: One becomes quieter as talk of living together nears, feeling both love and a sense of a closing door. Ambivalence is normal; hiding it is the risk, and saying it early is the kinder path.
graph_context: previous stage: First real friction
next stage: The honest conversation
